text:
deploy-bot: config-only deploy requested by @sara for change window 02:00-03:00 UTC. Changes: batching.window + timeout tuning + routing weight tweak. staged rollout requested (staged ramp). dry-run ok, runbook: https://go/runbooks/config-staged-rollback :gear:
sara: quick diff below — trying to reduce token-emission tail by increasing batching buffer but also tightening tenant concurrency to protect small pods. tiny surface area but two knobs changed so cautious rollout. yaml snippet:
```
service:
  batching:
    window_ms: 80
    buffer_tokens: 64
  routing:
    primary_route_weight: 0.92
    fallback_route_weight: 0.08
  limits:
    tenant_max_concurrency: 6
  timeouts:
    request_timeout_s: 9
```
tom: request pin for model so autoswitching doesn't affect canary: pin=rwd-v1.9-0308. also add telemetry for queue_depth and 429-rate. ops_maria will run preflight at 01:30 UTC.
ops_maria: preflight smoke done 01:33 UTC. basic latency check looks fine (p95 ~ 65ms). creating alerts: ALRT-4011 (queue depth increase), ALRT-4012 (429 spike), ALRT-4013 (p95 regression). will post every 10m during rollout.
pm_jake: heads-up for product impact: if we see 429 spikes we'll stop. prefer manual gating after final stage.
sara: rollout plan pasted: staged: 1% for 15m -> 10% for 20m -> 50% for 30m; hold for manual approval after final stage. rollback thresholds: ALRT-4012 or p95 delta >20ms. pin model as requested.
deploy-bot: accepted plan. starting staged rollout at 02:00 UTC. command: `@deploy-bot start --thread 1796604321 --stages 1:15m,10:20m,50:30m --pin rwd-v1.9-0308 --hold-after-final`
monitoring-bot: t+7m stage1: queue_depth +1. avg p95 +2ms. no alerts.
monitoring-bot: stage1 complete. promoting to stage2 (10%). t+5m into stage2: queue_depth +6, 429-rate 0.4%. approaching ALRT-4012 threshold.
tom: seeing traces — fallback route calls increasing, tenant_max_concurrency seems to be throttling some heavy tenants. ops_maria, recommend pause and investigate. :mag:
ops_maria: pausing promotion to stage3. holding at 10% and running targeted load tests against small-tenant pods. will try reverting routing weight only if needed.
monitoring-bot: t+18m stage2: 429-rate spikes to 1.8% -> firing ALRT-4012. p95 delta +28ms, ALRT-4013 fired too.
sara: aborting rollout. @deploy-bot rollback 1796604321-stage-run
pm_jake: concur — abort. product impact minimal but avoid customer-facing 429s.
deploy-bot: rollback started: reverting config to previous values. ETA ~90s. posting status.
monitoring-bot: post-rollback t+2m: queue_depth back to baseline, 429-rate <0.05%, p95 within 3ms of baseline. all alerts cleared.
ops_maria: root-cause notes: increasing batching.window combined with lowering tenant_max_concurrency created queue buildup on a subset of small-capacity pods, causing overload and increased fallback calls. routing weight tweak amplified fallback pressure.
tom: mitigation plan: split change into two separate deploys — (A) batching.window only (no routing or concurrency changes) at low daytime window; (B) routing weight + tenant concurrency in a separate subsequent deploy with staged capacity testing. keep model pin for both.
sara: agree. will open two PRs: PR-12890 (batching-only) and PR-12891 (routing+limits). schedule PR-12890 for tomorrow 09:00-10:00 UTC with 2% canary then 10% hold. ops_maria, please run expanded preflight for PR-12890.
ops_maria: noted. will add synthetic load focused on small-tenant patterns and watch ALRT-4011/4012 closely.
pm_jake: thanks all. please add a short release note: "Batching buffer increased to improve token throughput; split rollout to avoid routing-side regressions."
sara: tagging follow-up owner: @tom to own PR-12891 ramp plan. closing thread; next action: PRs and reschedule. :white_check_mark:
